passage: In the upstairs office above a hardware shop in Sirsa, Nazia pulled a sheet of chart paper across the table and drew four circles: sales, engineers, finance, and the shopkeepers who would use the billing tool. Beside sales she first wrote 'wants it fast', then crossed it out and wrote 'a rival demo is next month, afraid of losing two shops'. Beside the engineers: 'want it right' became 'tired of fixing the same bug after every rushed release'. Finance: 'low cost' became 'last quarter's overspend was questioned by the owner'. 'They aren't asking for opposite things,' she murmured, tapping the sheet. 'They're each afraid of something different.' Gurpreet, the tester, leaned in and added a note about the shopkeepers. Nazia pinned the sheet to the wall.

qa.q: What did Nazia write beside finance after crossing out 'low cost'?
qa.a: She wrote 'last quarter's overspend was questioned by the owner'.

qa.q: What does Nazia's murmur suggest she has realised?
qa.a: Nazia realises the groups are not asking for opposite things but fear different things, and she seems relieved and more hopeful.

qa.q: What other approach could Nazia use if the concerns still clash?
qa.a: Nazia could offer a smaller first release with a firm date for quality fixes, since it speaks to the speed, quality and cost worries together.

qa.q: How might the engineers see the map?
qa.a: They may feel heard, because the sheet records their tiredness of fixing the same bug and not just the word 'quality'.

grounding: Shows a project lead drawing the affected groups and writing each group's underlying concern beside its stated demand.

passage:
In a glass meeting room in Barcelona, Pablo stood at the whiteboard with three coloured markers. The launch date fight had been going on for two weeks. Soo-ah, the lead engineer, watched him draw three circles: Sales, Engineering, Finance.
Under each he wrote two lines. The first was what they kept saying. Sales: 'Launch in March.' Engineering: 'We need two more months.' Finance: 'No extra spending.' The second line was what they actually cared about. Sales: a big client's contract renews in April. Engineering: last year's rushed launch caused a month of night-time fixes. Finance: the budget review in May.
Soo-ah leaned forward. 'So Sales needs that one client happy by April, not the whole product.'
'Exactly,' Pablo said, and circled it.

qa.q: When does the big client's contract renew?
What does Soo-ah leaning forward suggest?
qa.a: It suggests Soo-ah felt interested and hopeful, seeing a way through the fight once the real concerns were written down.

qa.q: What else could Pablo do with the map?
qa.a: He could check each written concern with the groups themselves, so he isn't guessing, before proposing an option.

qa.q: How might the engineering team feel seeing their concern written down?
qa.a: The engineers may feel understood, since their fear of another month of night-time fixes is named instead of dismissed as slowness.

grounding: It shows a project lead mapping who is affected and writing each group's actual concern beneath its stated demand.

passage:
In the hospital's small IT room, Lalit had a new patient-registration system to deliver and three groups pulling at him. Himani from the finance office had come down to argue about cost again.
Instead of arguing, Lalit pulled a sheet of chart paper across the table. 'Let me draw who's in this.' Doctors, front-desk nurses, IT, finance. For each, he wrote what they had demanded in emails, then asked Himani to help him write what they really needed.
Front desk: 'a faster system' really meant shorter queues at 9 a.m. IT: 'more testing' really meant not losing patient records. Finance, Himani said, 'less money' really meant staying inside this year's grant.
Looking at the sheet, Lalit saw that the 9 a.m. queue could be eased with one extra registration screen, without touching the grant.

qa.q: What did 'a faster system' really mean for the front desk?
How might Himani have felt when Lalit asked for help instead of arguing?
qa.a: Himani probably felt surprised and respected, and more willing to explain finance's real concern.

qa.q: What could Lalit do next with the chart paper?
qa.a: He could show it to each group to confirm their real need, then propose the extra screen as a first step.

qa.q: How might the front-desk nurses be affected by this approach?
qa.a: Their daily pain, the 9 a.m. queue, becomes the target, so they may get relief sooner than through a full rebuild.

grounding: It shows a project lead mapping stakeholders and writing each group's actual concern rather than just their stated demand.
